docs.title: The Hungry Frontier — Rules & Mechanics
docs.text: Probably not a mimic.

docs.title: Purpose and Overview
docs.text:
As the Guides of the Hungry Frontier, we put forth this living document (probably not a mimic) to put into writing the rules, policies and guidelines that are to be used in the operation of the Hungry Frontier.

This document is to be kept up-to-date with the currently used Ruleset, House Rules, and Rules/Mechanics decisions used by the Hungry Frontier, its Guides and Players.

Any establishment of House/Table Rules, changes to the codified Official game rules or changes to the codified House/Table Rules will be listed in the following pages.

Any changes to the document will be made on a new line and have the date of the change saved at the end of the change, with any obsolete info being struck out, not deleted.

We reserve the rights to change these rules whenever.

docs.title: Update 01.26.2026
docs.text:
A. The following Rules and Mechanics were codified into the Frontier, using the sourcebooks from WotC's Dungeons and Dragons 2014 (hereafter called 5e) and WotC's Dungeons and Dragons 2024 (hereafter called 5.5e).

B. As of Monday, January 26, 2026 the Hungry Frontier will be using the general rules, equipment, spells, etc of Dungeons and Dragons 5.5 edition. If a rule or ability from 5e is missing or has not been rewritten then it, in most cases, may still be used.

docs.title: Frontier Guide Decisions regarding specific 5e/5.5e Rules & Cases
docs.text: It is the decision of the Hungry Frontier's Council of Guides that the following case decisions be implemented for the operation of the Hungry Frontier.

docs.title: Druid Wildshape Options — 01/28/2026
docs.text:
It is the decision of the Hungry Frontier's Council of Guides that all Druids may choose 5e Beast statblocks when deciding their wildshape forms. This is in large part due to 5.5e changing many statblocks' (mostly of large creatures) creature types from beast to another type, thereby limiting the pool of available choices.

The following creatures count as beasts for purposes of wildshape:

  • Owlbear
  • Hooded Viper Raptor — *see Guide Wood for stats

docs.title: Nick Weapon Mastery + Dual Wielder + Two Weapon Fighting Style + 5.5e Light Weapon Property
docs.text:
It is the decision of the Hungry Frontier's Council of Guides that the following properties/features interact in the following ways:

  1. Light Property: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative.

  2. Two-Weapon Fighting — Fighting Style Feat (Prerequisite: Fighting Style Feature): When you make an extra attack as a result of using a weapon that has the Light property, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of that attack if you aren't already adding it to the damage.

  3. Nick: When you make the extra attack of the Light property, you can make it as part of the Attack action instead of as a Bonus Action. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

  4. Dual Wielder — General Feat (Prerequisite: Level 4+, Strength or Dexterity 13+) — Enhanced Dual Wielding: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a weapon that has the Light property, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn with a different weapon, which must be a Melee weapon that lacks the Two-Handed property. You don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative.

docs.title: Interaction Breakdown
docs.text:
• Light + TWF: Gives Action Attack and Bonus Action Extra Attack (Light) both with damage modifiers (TWF). Both attacks need to be with separate light weapons.
  • Light + TWF + Nick: Gives Attack and Extra Attack (Light) as part of Action (Nick) both with damage modifiers (TWF), leaving Bonus Action available. Both attacks need to be with separate light weapons.
  • Light + TWF + Nick + DW: Gives Attack and Extra Attack (Light) as part of Action (Nick) both with modifiers (TWF). Both attacks need to be with separate light weapons. And Bonus Action may be used to make an Extra Attack (DW) without damage modifiers with any non-2H weapon.

In Conclusion

Using both your Action and Bonus Action you may make up to 3 attacks total, with the complete combo.

docs.title: Casting Multiple Spells in one turn — 06/17/2026
docs.text:
Located in the Player's Handbook, Chapter 7: Spells, is the excerpt:

One Spell with a Spell Slot per Turn

On a turn, you can expend only one spell slot to cast a spell. This rule means you can't, for example, cast a spell with a spell slot using the Magic action and another one using a Bonus Action on the same turn.

docs.title: Frontier Clarification
docs.text:
Rules as Written this means that if you have access to a "Free Use" of a spell in which you do not have to use a spell slot [e.g., Magic Initiate, the Paladin's Smite feature, etc] you may cast another spell that uses or expends a spell slot. And of course cantrips which don't take spell slots anyway.

When in doubt

See if the feature says "You can cast it once without a spell slot…".

docs.title: Frontier Character Death and Retirement Rules
docs.text:
There are three death options. Once a player character hits 0 Hit Points, they have until their next turn to choose one of the following options:

Death Option Immediate Effect / Process Resulting Effect I Don't Want To Die The PC is immediately stabilized at 0HP and returned to town. PC is frightened of whatever caused their death. -2 to all d20 rolls until the next full level up. Death Saving Throws See Chapter 1 of the Player's Handbook for the rules. Death of the PC allows you to make a new PC using 35% of the dead PC's session XP (rounded up). Blaze of Glory The dying PC may take an immediate turn outside of initiative order. All attack rolls hit and count as a Critical Hit. They then immediately die, and may not be resurrected or healed. Death of the PC allows you to make a new PC using 25% of the dead PC's session XP (rounded up).

Update — 05.07.2026

XP from a PC killed in combat may be used towards an existing player character that is below level 5.

docs.title: Massive Damage / Instant Death
docs.text:
When a PC takes enough damage that it brings them passed 0 HP and their negative Max HP, they have 1 round to choose one of the following options:

  1. I Don't Want To Die: Same as above.
  2. Blaze of Glory: Same as above.

docs.title: Retirement of a PC
docs.text:
A player may choose to retire a player character at any time. That PC then either returns east or becomes an NPC in town, either path means that PC is no longer playable. They are considered to be happy, healthy, and mostly safe wherever they chose to settle.

If a player chooses to retire a PC, they may make a new character at 50% of the retired PC's session XP (rounded up). This is called Inherited XP.

docs.title: Downtime Activities, including Crafting
docs.text: Downtime in the Hungry Frontier is drawn from a number of official D&D sources: Downtime Activities in Xanathar's Guide to Everything, Crafting Equipment in the Player's Handbook, and Crafting Magical Items in the Dungeon Master's Guide.

docs.title: Downtime Activities
docs.text:
Xanathar's Guide to Everything, Chapter 2 — Downtime Revisited

  • Many activities take a number of days; an 8 hour day, generally a workweek [5 days] or more, to complete.
  • Activities call for both gold and days to be used in completing the activity. With some requiring skill checks to determine success.
  • If an activity requires the use of a tool, you (the PC) must be proficient in the tool being used.

docs.title: List of available activities in the Frontier
docs.text: Activity Skill Check Tool Used Cost Description Carousing Persuasion n/a 10 / 50 / 250 gp, 1 Workweek Make contacts in a town or settlement. Gambling Insight, Deception, and Intimidation Game Set (may replace one Skill) 10–1000 gp, 1 Workweek Partake in games of chance to win a fortune… or lose one. Relaxation n/a n/a 7 Days Relax and/or recover from non-magical afflictions. Religious Service Religion or Persuasion n/a 1 Workweek Partake in service to a temple/church. docs.title: Crafting Equipment
docs.text:
Player's Handbook, Chapter 6 — Equipment

To craft a nonmagical item, you need tools, raw materials, and time, each of which is detailed below. If you meet the requirements, you make the item, and you can use it or sell it at its normal price.

Tools. See the Tools section located in Chapter 6 to see what items can be made with certain tools. If an item isn't listed, it is up to the Guide to determine which tool set is required for the crafting project. All characters involved in the activity must have proficiency in the tool set being used.

Costs. You need enough raw materials equal to half the item's market value in gold pieces. The activity will also require a number of days equal to the item's market value divided by 10 (rounded up to the nearest day). The Guide determines whether appropriate raw materials are available.

Assisting in Crafting. Characters can combine their efforts to shorten the crafting time. Divide the time needed to create an item by the number of characters working on it. Normally, only one other character can assist you, but the DM might allow more assistants. The time needed cannot be shortened to less than 1 day.

docs.title: Scribing a Spell Scroll
docs.text:
Prerequisites. Proficiency in the Arcana skill or with the Calligrapher's Supplies and must have the spell prepared each day of the inscription. You must also have any material components required by a spell; if the spell consumes the components they are consumed when you finish the inscription. The Scroll's spell uses the character's Spell Save DC and Spell Attack Bonus. In the case of Cantrips, the spell acts using the level of the Inscriber.

Cost. See table below.

Spell Level Time Cost Cantrip 1 day 15 GP 1 1 day 25 GP 2 3 days 100 GP 3 5 days 150 GP 4 10 days 1,000 GP 5 25 days 1,500 GP 6 40 days 10,000 GP 7 50 days 12,500 GP

docs.title: Brewing Potions of Healing
docs.text: A character who has proficiency with the Herbalism Kit can create a Potion of Healing. Doing so requires using that kit and 25 GP of raw material over the course of 1 day (8 hours of work).

docs.title: Crafting Magical Items
docs.text:
Dungeon Master's Guide, Chapter 7 — Treasure

Project Source. At the Guide's discretion, a PC may require a Project Source; anything that gives the player character the knowledge to start the process of crafting a magical item. This can take the form of written information (a book, scroll, schematic, and so forth), an expert tutor with wisdom to share, a master artisan with skills to teach, a supernatural manifestation of the project's scope and secrets, or any other form of the Guide's determination.

Arcana Proficiency. You and any assistants must have proficiency in the Arcana skill.

Tools. See table below. You must use the required tool to make an item and have proficiency with that tool. Any assistants must also have proficiency with it.

Item Category Required Tool Armor Leatherworker's Tools, Smith's Tools, or Weaver's Tools *depending on the kind of armor as noted in the tools' descriptions Potion Alchemist's Supplies or Herbalism Kit Ring Jeweler's Tools Rod Woodcarver's Tools Scroll Calligrapher's Supplies Staff Woodcarver's Tools Wand Woodcarver's Tools Weapon Leatherworker's Tools, Smith's Tools, or Woodcarver's Tools *depending on the kind of weapon as noted in the tools' descriptions Wondrous Item Tinker's Tools or the tool required to make the nonmagical item on which the magic item is based

Spells. If a magic item allows its user to cast any spells from it, you must have all those spells prepared every day you spend crafting the item.

Work per Day. For each day of crafting, you must work for 8 hours. If an item requires multiple days, those days needn't be consecutive.

Assistants. Characters can combine their efforts to shorten the crafting time. Divide the time needed to create an item by the number of characters working on it. Normally, only one other character can assist you, but the DM might allow more assistants. The time needed cannot be shortened to less than 1 day.

docs.title: Time and Cost
docs.text:
Item Rarity Time* Cost* Common 5 days 50 GP Uncommon 10 days 200 GP Rare 50 days 2,000 GP Very Rare 125 days 20,000 GP Legendary 250 days 100,000 GP

* The time and cost are halved for a consumable item other than a Spell Scroll, whose crafting time and cost are given in the Player's Handbook.

Raw Materials. The cost in the table represents the raw materials needed to make a magic item. The DM determines whether appropriate raw materials are available.

If a magic item incorporates an item that has a purchase cost (such as a weapon or a suit of armor), you must also pay that entire cost or craft that item using the rules in the Player's Handbook. For example, to make +1 Armor (Plate Armor), you must pay 3,500 GP or pay 2,000 GP and craft the armor.

Guide's Discretion — 05/26/2026

Currently only magic items from Frontier Legal Books may be crafted, at Guide's Discretion.

docs.title: How to Downtime in the Frontier
What is Downtime?
docs.text: Downtime is that period between adventures and expeditions, the long rest(s) spent in town, the time spent recuperating after a crazy outing in the Wilds of the Frontier. Downtime allows player characters to pursue side interests between adventures and also encourages players to become more invested in the campaign world.

docs.title: How to use Downtime in the Frontier?
docs.text:
All downtime activities make use of two currencies, gold pieces (gp) and days, which are acquired from playing in a session. These currencies can then be spent in the 3 Downtime Markets found in the marketplace located in the westmarches app:

  • Frontier Sabbatical: downtime activities like gambling, research and training.
  • Community Crafting District: crafting mundane items and equipment and brewing potions of healing.
  • Premium Crafting Workshops: crafting magical items, brewing potions and scribing spell scrolls.

Most activities require a third currency in order to be spent, the Downtime Token. The downtime token (like a magic shop token) is needed for activities requiring the attention of a Guide either due to needing a skill check or due to a prolonged process.

To request a downtime token, create a thread in Crafting District and Recreations with the title being your Player Character's name. Then you may comment your request along with any future downtime activities within that thread for that character. Please make a separate Thread for each Player Character.

docs.title: How to Roll?
docs.text: We will be utilizing the Avrae bot to help us roll within discord. When prompted by a Guide, input !roll then the die being used, generally 1d20. The Avrae bot will roll for you and display it immediately. You comment your total to the Guide and viola! Downtime completed.

docs.title: How to get Days?
docs.text:
Currently there are two ways to accumulate days:

  1. You earn 3 days at the end of every session.
  2. You can earn 3 days for writing an adventure journal for that session.

docs.title: Removal of the Optional Rule: Flanking
docs.text: The Hungry Frontier will no longer be using the Optional Rule: Flanking from DMG14 → Ch 8.

docs.title: Potions of Healing
docs.text:
Rules as written, a potion can be drunk or administered as a Bonus Action to then roll for HP applied.

Campaign Rule

In addition, you may use an Action to either drink or administer and receive the maximum amount of HP without rolling.

docs.title: Hold Action
docs.text:
Campaign Rule

On your turn you may choose to permanently change your initiative slot in an encounter to a lower slot. This can only be done once per character per encounter. Once the Initiative is changed it cannot be undone, unless a class/subclass feature, feat or spell allows you to change it.

docs.title: Critical Hits
docs.text:
Campaign Rule

When a Natural 20 is rolled on an attack roll (Melee, Ranged or Spell), use the following changes:

Melee, Ranged and Spell Attack Rolls: Roll all applicable damage dice for the attack and add applicable modifiers. Then add the Maximum damage of all applicable damage dice to the total.

docs.title: Languages in the Frontier
docs.text:
D&D 5.5e classifies Languages into two categories: Standard and Rare.

Campaign Rule

We will be adding a third category: Frontier Languages. These are languages spoken by the creatures of Okeron, once lost to time. Their languages are generally spoken by the current natives of the west or are dead languages of the societies that once dwelt here in the west.

These languages may be learned by a player character as part of a downtime activity, if they have a suitable teacher to learn from.

Language Name Who Speaks / Spoke It Description Okernian (Ancient Common) The language of the ancient empire of the west. Dead language mostly found in old texts. Xlatui (Ancient Orcish) Orc tribes of the Southwest Corridor, Yuan-ti The cousin of modern Orcish, although mainly reserved for traditional ceremony. Those who speak orcish can generally understand Xlatui. Poquat (Tortle) Tortles, other species in the SWC A pidgin language with borrowed words from dwarves, orcs and ancient humans. Spoken in the Southwest Corridor. Nek'eow Tabaxi A mix of vocalizations, body postures and scent marking. Cats understand it but don't let on. WIP-Lizardic Lizardfolk A mix of mostly body language accented by hisses, clicks and chirps as well as chemical signaling. Thaehanti Tiefling Draws from infernal, abyssal and okernian.

docs.title: Long and Short Rests
docs.text:
The Hungry Frontier will use a west march method of Resting, this means that Long Rests may only be taken in the safety of town.

Rules for both Long Rests and Short Rests can be found in the PHB24 Rules Glossary, with the following changes:

  • Short Rests can be taken any place of relative safety, and last anywhere from 1 hour (within Dungeons) to 8 hours (Day to Day).
  • Long Rests can only be taken in the safety of town, and last anywhere from 8 hours to multiple days.

After a session it is assumed your character immediately takes a long rest upon reaching town, the only exception is for player characters playing back to back sessions (same day and/or consecutive days).

Subject to change

We reserve the right to change these rules as we see fits best for the Hungry Frontier.

docs.title: Sidekicking
docs.text:
A Player Character may temporarily play at a higher level in a session by sidekicking. In order to sidekick, a side kicking player character must have a Mentor, another player character at least 3 levels higher.

  • While mentored the side kick uses the proficiency bonus of the Mentor. This will generally affect most d20 Tests.
  • The side kick also gains a number of hit dice, of their own class, up to their Mentor's level minus 1. They may take the Fixed value (shown in PHB24 → Level Advancement) or roll these Hit Dice and add their Constitution modifier a number of times equal to the number of Hit Dice rolled.

For the side kick to keep these bonuses, the Side Kick and their Mentor must stay within 180 ft of each other.

Worked Example

Mentor — Wizard Lvl 9, proficiency bonus: +4 Side Kick — Fighter Lvl 4, hit dice: d10, +2 CON modifier

While within 180 ft of the wizard, the fighter's proficiency bonus becomes +4 instead of their normal +2.

The fighter also gains 4 more hit dice and 4× their CON modifier. In this case it would be 4d10 + 8. Using the fixed value for fighters, the Side Kick gains (6 + 6 + 6 + 6 + 8) = 32 HP for that session.

docs.title: Class Hit Dice
docs.text: Class Hit Dice Average Barbarian d12 7 Fighter, Paladin, Ranger d10 6 Bard, Cleric, Druid, Monk, Rogue, Warlock d8 5 Sorcerer, Wizard d6 4

docs.title: Companions, Summoned Creatures, and Similar — Update 02.07.2026
docs.text:
Campaign Rule Addition

Regarding Animal Companions, Summoned Creatures and similar Companions that rely on a Player Character's level and/or proficiency bonus.

When a Player Character is side kicked up by a mentor (see Side kicking Rules above) and that PC has a companion that uses the PC's proficiency bonus (PB) or level for its stats (e.g., Artificer-Steel Defender, Ranger-Animal Companion, etc.), the side kicking PC uses their side-kicked PB or Level (mentor's minus 1) to determine that companion's stats.

docs.title: Hungry Dragon Store Coin / Gift Card
docs.text:
Store Coin / Gift Card may be used as an extra use of Heroic Inspiration. Limit to one coin per player, per session.

Like Heroic Inspiration, Store Coins may not be traded or given to other players.

Reference

See the Player's Handbook 5.5e → Rules Glossary for more information on Heroic Inspiration.

docs.title: Waiver of Session XP
docs.text:
Want to keep your character within a certain level range? Are all your friends just now joining the Frontier? Do you just really like how a peculiar Guide runs Intro sessions? Or do the deadly challenges that face a lower level character call like a siren to you?

For whatever reason, if you do not want to be rewarded XP after a session, you must let that Session's Guide know before the end of the session and you part ways. In doing this you are waiving the XP reward for that session:

  • It does not get stored, tracked or banked for later use.
  • It cannot be applied to another player character.
  • It is lost to the Wild Frontier, gone for good.

In this way you can stay at whatever level you wish, for however long you wish.

docs.title: Regarding Character Creation of 5e, 5.5e and Mixed Player Characters
docs.text:
Reminder

Use of Weapon Mastery is a 5.5e Class Feature and only available to Classes that gain that feature.

docs.title: Only 5e
docs.text: If making or running a full 5e character, you may only choose from Frontier legal 5e Character Options (Feats, Class/Subclass Features, etc). 5e only characters may use the Optional Class Features in Tasha's Cauldron of Everything when making a character. However, spells and equipment will be based upon the 5.5e ruleset.

docs.title: Only 5.5e
docs.text: If making or running a full 5.5e character, you may only choose from any Frontier legal 5.5e Character Options (Feats, Class/Subclass Features, etc).

docs.title: Mixed Character Options
docs.text:
When making a 5.5e character, you may choose a Frontier Legal 5e Subclass or Species to go with your 5.5e Class, unless it has an updated 5.5e version of the same name (see Species and Classes/Subclasses of the Frontier for more). Changes to allow for compatibility must be made and are laid out in the 5.5e Ruleset. Consult a Frontier Guide for review (which may or may not include approval of the player character).

5e Feats and Mixed Characters

5e Feats may not be used with 5.5e material. If a 5e character option lets you choose a feat, mixed characters may choose a general feat from 5.5e.

docs.title: Transitioning 5e Characters to 5.5e
docs.text:
If transitioning a character from 5e to 5.5e, you must transition as much as mechanically possible. If an option is not currently in 5.5e then you may keep using the 5e version of that character option [Character Options mean Subclasses, Feats, Backgrounds, and/or Species]. However some changes may be necessary to keep character cohesion. Keep in mind not all character options, abilities, etc will stay the same when transitioning.

  • When transitioning and only when transitioning, you may change the background of your PC to better fit 5.5e ASI restrictions and character vision.
  • REMINDER! Transition is not mandatory, however if you choose to transition a character from 5e to 5.5e you must do so as completely as possible.

docs.title: Multiclassing
docs.text:
No Cross-Ruleset Multiclassing

Multiclassing between rulesets is not allowed.

docs.title: Sub-Sections
docs.text:
• 5e to 5.5e Transition Rules
  • Character Respec

docs.title: Player Character Respec
docs.text:
Respec allows a player to adjust a pre-existing player character to correct a mistake in design from early development or to make a change that would allow that character to be more fun to play. A respec allows you to change most choices in a character, but your character's name, species, and class must remain the same.

Not a Rebuild

Respecs are not a method to completely make a new character at your current level. Your character's identity should remain intact.

docs.title: Level Thresholds
docs.text:
• Levels 1–3: a player may adjust their character's features as much as they like until that character reaches Level 4.
  • At Level 6 every character gets One Free Respec which may be kept and used at a later level.

In-Party Adjustments

Follow the rules below for what can and can not be respec'ed. Often we don't see a mistake until we are at the table. This will help players new and old make adjustments in the early levels.

docs.title: What Can Be Changed
docs.text:
With a respec you can change:

  • Ability Scores
  • ASI
  • Backgrounds
  • Multi-Class Levels
  • Feats
  • Languages
  • Skills
  • Subclasses

docs.title: What Cannot Be Changed
docs.text:
You can not change:

  • Species
  • Class
  • (Wizard) Spellbooks

docs.title: Respecing when Multiclassed
docs.text:
You can change levels in a multiclass or remove the extra class. You cannot change or remove your Primary class and your multiclass level can not match or exceed your primary class level.

Your primary class is the class with the highest level. If both classes are of the same level at time of respec, you can choose either to be your primary class.

docs.title: 5e to 5.5e Transition Rules
docs.text:
The following will be the Guiding Standard when it comes to 5e-5.5e Rule Interactions and PC Transitions.

  1. Frontier Guides (DM) have the final say.
  2. Unless stated otherwise we are using the D&D 5.5e ruleset for all characters as well as including, but not limited to 5.5e Equipment, Magic Items, Spells, etc.
  3. 5e Player Characters are still playable, but may only use 5e Character Options. See the Character Creation Rules for more information.
  4. Objections or changes will be dealt with on a case by case basis, final decisions will ultimately be up to the Guides (see Rule 1).

docs.title: Transitions and Making a Character
docs.text:
Transitioning your Player Character is not Mandatory.

Transitioning a Player Character means that an existing 5e Frontier character is changing, as far as mechanically possible, to 5.5e. This means and generally starts with taking the same class, subclass, species and background as the original character and rebuilding, as close as possible, a replica of the original character.

In some cases, due to 5.5e initial ASI restrictions and other new rules/mechanics some features available to 5e characters will not be the same or available as a 5.5e character. To help smooth the transition process, you are allowed to change the background of your Player Character to one that better fits the feel or mechanics of the original character.

Transitioning is not a free re-spec of a player character. It does not allow you to swap or drastically change your original character's class, subclass, or species. If transitioning a player character does not fulfill your original vision of the character, then you do not need to transition and may continue to play that PC in its 5e version.

Permanent Change

Once a player character is transitioned it is a permanent change and the original player character is no longer allowed, without prior Guide review.

docs.title: Player Character Transition Rollback — aka Rollback
docs.text:
So, you want to transition your 5e character to 5.5e, but you're concerned you won't enjoy the new features as much. You now have the option to rollback your character, but it will require some planning ahead on your part.

  1. Before you transition your character you must declare to a Guide that you would like to have the option to rollback your transitioned character to 5e 2014 rules.
  2. You must then submit a current non-transitioned 5e version of your character sheet before starting the process of transitioning to 5.5e.
  3. You have 2 sessions to decide if you would like to continue with your new 5.5e character build or rollback your transitioned character to your 5e version.

docs.title: Notes on Custom Backgrounds
docs.text:
5e Customized Background

Customized backgrounds are available for use in the Frontier. Allowing you to choose a background, swap its background's feature, choose any two skills, and choose a total of two tool proficiencies or languages from the sample backgrounds. You may choose to take the original background's starting equipment. [found in the PHB14 → Ch.4 under Customizing Backgrounds].

5.5e Custom Background

Customized Backgrounds are available for use in the Frontier. This allows you to choose which Ability Scores gain an Increase (+2/+1 or +1/+1/+1), choose an origin feat, choose two skills and a tool proficiency, and receive 50 gp. [Described in the DMG24 → Ch 3 and the PHB24 → Ch 2 & 4].

Consult a Guide

It is highly recommended that any customized content be consulted on by a Hungry Frontier Guide.

docs.title: Converting a 5e Background into 5.5e
docs.text:
"Backgrounds in older D&D books don't include ability score adjustments. If you're using a background from an older book, adjust your ability scores by increasing one score by 2 and a different one by 1, or increase three scores by 1. None of these increases can raise a score above 20."

"Also, if the background you choose doesn't provide a feat, you gain an Origin feat of your choice."

As described in the PHB24 → Ch 2.

docs.title: Species Categories
docs.text:
Default Species: Found regularly throughout Selardor, with many coming to Merzileta from the East. These ancestries are usable by all players in the Frontier.

Common Species: Found only on or near the western continent of Okeron. These ancestries have been unlocked through in-game negotiations and diplomacy. These ancestries are usable by all players in the Frontier.

Uncommon Species: Newly discovered species found only in Okeron or on other Planes. These ancestries can only be used after a player has completed a specific mission to aid their people.

docs.title: Regarding Custom Lineage and Human Variant
docs.text:
Human Variant

Due to 5.5e Human being the new ruleset's equivalent, and 5e feats are not allowed with 5.5e characters, Human Variant is solely allowed for 5e Only player characters [see Character Creation Rules for 5e Only PCs].

Custom Lineage

While similar to Human Variant, Custom Lineage (found in Tasha's Cauldron of Everything, Chapter 1) is available for 5.5e or Mixed PCs with the following changes:

  • Remove the Ability Score Increase.
  • Only 5.5e Origin Feats can be chosen for the species' given Feat.

For any player choosing this species, the image/description of the character's species must align with one of the Frontier Legal Species.
